newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh resumes peace talks with tribal rebels.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh resumes peace talks with tribal rebels.

text.p: The government of Bangladesh on Monday resumed peace talks in Dhaka with tribal rebels fighting for autonomy for the Chittagong Hill Tracts in the country's southeast.

"Talks will continue tomorrow (Tuesday) because consensus on some contentious issues has yet to be reached," Aitur Rahman, an official of the special affairs division which deals with Hill Tracts issues, told reporters after five hours of talks.
The parliamentary chief whip of the ruling Awami League, Abul Hasnat Abdullah, led the government side at the talks while the rebel side was headed by Jyotirindra Budhipriya Larma.
Larma is the head of Parbattya Chattagram Jana Sanghati Samity (PCJSS), the political wing of the tribal Shanti Bahini guerrillas.

Earlier on Monday, Larma and his comrades were flown to the capital city by a military helicopter from Dudukchhari, a remote tribal hamlet in Khagrachhari hill district bordering India's northeastern Tripura state.
Monday's session was the fifth meeting between the government and the PCJSS since Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina began a fresh attempt to end the 23-year-old insurgency.

Officials said broad outlines of a treaty had already been agreed at talks between the two sides in May, but the PCJSS was facing opposition from a group of Shanti Bahini hardliners and the Hill Students Council, which backs the insurgency.

Shanti Bahini started the insurgency in 1973 to try to secure autonomy for the 5,500 sq mile (14,200 sq km) Hill Tracts, bordering India and Burma, and the expulsion of some 500,000 Bengali-speaking settlers from the region.
Over 8,500 rebels, soldiers and civilians have been killed in the protracted bush war, which also forced some 50,000 tribespeople to flee to Tripura.
Nearly 7,000 refugees returned home in March and April following an agreement between Dhaka and New Delhi, but officials say it remains uncertain when the next phase of repatriation will start.
